{t:"一、詞彙題",n:[["claim a prize","領取獎金；claim 也可作「聲稱、索賠」。"],["foot the bill","慣用語：付帳。foot 作動詞＝支付。"],["win by a margin of…","以…的差距獲勝；margin 另有「頁邊、利潤」。"],["mutual","相互的、共同的：mutual agreement / respect / friend。"],["assume the responsibility","承擔責任（新接下）；對比 maintain＝維持既有的。"],["trigger","n. 誘因／v. 引發：trigger allergic reactions。"]],q:[
[1,"The lottery winner has exactly ninety days to ___ their multi-million-dollar prize before the ticket expires.",["claim","harvest","profit","reserve"],0,"claim a prize＝領取獎金；ticket expires 表示須在期限內領獎。"],
[2,"After entering the workforce, many young graduates realize that the corporate world can be a competitive ___, where employees fight for limited opportunities and recognition.",["jungle","landscape","territory","region"],0,"jungle 比喻弱肉強食、競爭激烈的環境。"],
[3,"The researcher paid ___ attention to the small changes in temperature during the experiment, as even slight differences could affect the final results.",["grave","particular","peculiar","negative"],1,"pay particular attention＝特別留意；後句 even slight differences 呼應。"],
[4,"The current mayor won the election by a ___ of only 1,000 votes, so the opposing side immediately demanded a careful recount.",["fraction","bunch","margin","summary"],2,"win by a margin of…＝以…的差距獲勝。"],
[5,"After long discussions, the two rival companies finally reached a ___ agreement to share the patent rights.",["keen","modest","mutual","hasty"],2,"mutual agreement＝雙方都同意的共識。"],
[6,"For some patients, certain foods—such as shrimp or crab—can be a kind of ___ for severe allergic reactions in daily life.",["agency","offense","remedy","trigger"],3,"trigger＝引發過敏反應的誘因。"],
[7,"Following the natural disaster, local volunteers ___ the responsibility of distributing supplies to affected families.",["observed","maintained","guaranteed","assumed"],3,"assume the responsibility＝承擔責任（災後才開始的新任務）；maintained 指持續既有職責，不精準。"],
[8,"The poll is only meaningful if the respondents are ___. If we only survey senior citizens, we won’t get a full picture of what the people actually need.",["representative","cooperative","consistent","authentic"],0,"只調查老年人不夠全面，受訪者須具「代表性」。"],
[9,"The landlord refused to ___ the bill for the repairs even though the water pipe had been leaking for weeks.",["fold","foot","hand","dispute"],1,"foot the bill＝付帳、買單（慣用語）。"],
[10,"As a leader who values each team member’s input, Jennifer ___ listened to their concerns before making the final decision on the project.",["verbally","suspiciously","furiously","earnestly"],3,"values each member’s input → 誠懇地聆聽 earnestly。"]]},
{t:"二、綜合測驗",p:"<b>【11–15】</b><br>Ticket scalping, or reselling tickets at higher prices, is by no means a modern problem. In the late 1860s, for instance, the British novelist Charles Dickens toured the United States, giving public readings from his works to large audiences. Ticket resellers bought seats in bulk to create <u>(11)</u>, so disappointed fans who couldn’t find tickets had to pay sky-high prices on the street.<br>This is what economists call arbitrage—profiting from price differences between markets. In the primary market, ticket prices do not always reflect demand. To maintain a fair image and encourage sell-outs, event promoters often keep prices <u>(12)</u> low. Scalpers then buy up the limited tickets and resell them at higher prices on the secondary market.<br>While the practice remains acceptable in many regions, governments and the entertainment industry have begun to <u>(13)</u>. The U.S. BOTS Act bans scalping software, and Australia has capped resale prices to protect fans. Meanwhile, some performers have <u>(14)</u> tougher measures like “Verified Fan” systems to prioritize genuine followers over automated bots.<br>Despite these efforts, the battle continues. As long as demand for major events <u>(15)</u> supply, scalpers will likely find new loopholes, leaving the industry to balance free-market principles with fairness.<br><br><b>【16–20】</b><br>Bento, a traditional Japanese lunchbox, has a long history that reflects both practicality and cultural values. Its origins date back to the Kamakura period, when travelers carried dried rice for convenience. Over time, bento gradually <u>(16)</u> a carefully arranged meal. By the Edo period, it <u>(17)</u> an essential part of leisure activities, as people enjoyed it during occasions such as flower viewing and theater outings.<br>However, bento cannot be <u>(18)</u> to a simple meal. It also serves to express personal feelings and emotional connection. In many Japanese families, parents prepare bento for their children, often arranging the food with great care and creativity. This <u>(19)</u> not only enhances the visual appeal of the meal but also conveys a sense of love and dedication.<br>In recent years, with the growing influence of social media, beautifully arranged lunchboxes have attracted global interest. As a result, bento has become both a cultural symbol and a <u>(20)</u> trend, especially among younger generations who share their creations online and turn everyday meals into a form of artistic expression. It is valued for its convenience as well as the meaning and creativity it represents.",n:[["arbitrage","套利：從不同市場的價差獲利。"],["by no means","絕不、一點也不（＝not at all）。"],["scalp / loophole","scalp＝倒賣（黃牛票）；loophole＝法律漏洞。"],["opt for + N","選擇採用；opt to + V 亦可。"],["句型：By + 過去時間 + had p.p.","By the Edo period, it had become…：到那個過去時間點之前已完成 → 過去完成式（第 17 題）。"],["be reduced to…","被簡化為…（第 18 題）；regard 需搭 as，此處前無 as，故不選。"],["句型：not only…but also…","This attention to detail not only enhances… but also conveys…：對等連接兩個動詞片語。"],["date back to","追溯至（Its origins date back to…）。"]],q:[
"P0",[11,"（黃牛票）Ticket resellers bought seats in bulk to create ___, so disappointed fans had to pay sky-high prices.",["a legal privilege","an artificial shortage","an instant classic","a sudden surplus"],1,"大量買下座位 → 刻意造成的「人為短缺」。"],
[12,"Event promoters often keep prices ___ low to maintain a fair image and encourage sell-outs.",["deliberately","efficiently","immediately","reportedly"],0,"有明確目的 → 「刻意地」壓低票價。"],
[13,"Governments and the entertainment industry have begun to ___. The U.S. BOTS Act bans scalping software…",["tax ticket resales","expand ticket supply","limit ticket scalping","standardize ticket prices"],2,"後文各項措施的共同目的皆為「限制黃牛」。"],
[14,"Some performers have ___ tougher measures like “Verified Fan” systems.",["taken on","run into","opted for","checked out"],2,"opt for＋N＝選擇採用。"],
[15,"As long as demand for major events ___ supply, scalpers will likely find new loopholes.",["generates","diminishes","justifies","exceeds"],3,"demand exceeds supply＝需求超過供給。"],
"P1",[16,"（便當）Over time, bento gradually ___ a carefully arranged meal.",["derived from","succeeded to","prevailed in","evolved into"],3,"隨時間「演變成」精心擺設的餐點。"],
[17,"By the Edo period, it ___ an essential part of leisure activities.",["was to become","had become","would become","might become"],1,"By the Edo period 表示在該時間之前已完成 → 過去完成式。"],
[18,"Bento cannot be ___ to a simple meal.",["regarded","misled","weakened","reduced"],3,"be reduced to…＝被簡化成…。"],
[19,"Parents arrange food with great care. This ___ not only enhances the visual appeal…",["knowledge of cooking","focus on quantity","attention to detail","passion for taste"],2,"with great care and creativity → 對「細節的注重」。"],
[20,"Bento has become both a cultural symbol and a ___ trend, especially among younger generations.",["contemporary","considerable","compulsory","controversial"],0,"In recent years、social media → 「當代的」潮流。"]]},
{t:"三、文意選填",n:[["appoint A as B","任命 A 為 B：a woman appointed as her interpreter（過去分詞後置修飾 woman）。"],["less like A and more like B","與其說像 A，不如說像 B：silence seems less like coldness and more like self-protection。"],["Frustrated by…, Chizuko…","分詞構句（原為 Because she is frustrated…），主詞同為 Chizuko。"],["whether love can truly thrive when one side holds more power…","whether 引導名詞子句作 questions 的受詞；when 為時間／條件副詞子句。"],["thrive / pull off / grasp","thrive 蓬勃發展；pull off 成功完成（困難之事）；grasp 理解、掌握。"],["gain recognition","獲得肯定；recognition 亦為「認出」。"]],c:"《臺灣漫遊錄》（Taiwan Travelogue）：1938 年日治時期，日本作家青山千鶴子來臺，與臺灣女子千鶴相遇。選項庫共用 (A)–(J)。",q:[
"<b>【21–30】</b>\n<i>Taiwan Travelogue</i> is written by the Taiwanese author Shuang-zi Yang and translated into English by Lin King. Set in 1938 during Japanese rule in Taiwan, the novel [21] Aoyama Chizuko, a young Japanese novelist visiting Taiwan on a cultural tour. During her stay, she meets Chizuru, a Taiwanese woman appointed as her interpreter. Although their relationship begins as a [22] arrangement, the two women gradually become closer through shared experiences. These experiences build a stronger emotional connection between them and encourage Chizuko to learn more about her new friend.\nAs time passes, Chizuko becomes increasingly fascinated by Chizuru. However, Chizuru remains [23] and keeps many of her thoughts hidden. She never fully lets Chizuko enter her private world. She seldom [24] about her past, making it difficult for anyone to know her well. Frustrated by Chizuru’s unwillingness to share her feelings, Chizuko [25] to understand the reasons behind her behavior. As their journey nears its end, Chizuru’s silence starts to seem less like coldness and more like self-protection. At that moment, Chizuko begins to [26] what Chizuru has been trying to keep to herself.\nAt its heart, the novel questions whether love can truly [27] when one side holds more power than the other. The unequal relationship between Japan and Taiwan creates constant [28] even though the two women share genuine affection.\nThe novel gained widespread [29] in Taiwan after winning the International Booker Prize 2026, making it the first Taiwanese novel ever to receive the award. What makes the work especially impressive is that it successfully [30] two goals at once: telling a moving love story while encouraging readers to reflect on history, language, and power. Its international success has also brought greater attention to Taiwanese literature and its unique historical experiences.",[21,"the novel ___ Aoyama Chizuko, a young Japanese novelist visiting Taiwan",B1,4,"The novel follows＋人物＝小說以…為主角發展。"],
[22,"the relationship begins as a ___ arrangement (appointed as her interpreter)",B1,8,"被指派為口譯 → 工作上的「正式」安排，與後來的親近對比。"],
[23,"Chizuru remains ___ and keeps many of her thoughts hidden.",B1,3,"remain＋形容詞；想法隱藏 → 保持「疏離」distant。"],
[24,"She seldom ___ about her past.",B1,7,"open up about＝對…敞開心房。"],
[25,"Frustrated by Chizuru’s unwillingness, Chizuko ___ to understand the reasons.",B1,6,"struggle to V＝艱難地嘗試。"],
[26,"Chizuko begins to ___ what Chizuru has been trying to keep to herself.",B1,9,"grasp＝理解，呼應 silence 其實是自我保護。"],
[27,"Whether love can truly ___ when one side holds more power than the other.",B1,1,"love thrive＝愛情能否順利發展。"],
[28,"The unequal relationship creates constant ___.",B1,0,"不平等關係 → 持續的「緊張」tension。"],
[29,"The novel gained widespread ___ in Taiwan after winning the International Booker Prize 2026.",B1,5,"gain recognition＝獲得肯定。"],
[30,"It successfully ___ two goals at once.",B1,2,"pull off＝成功達成。"]]},
{t:"四、篇章結構",n:[["treat them less as tools and more as social partners","less as A and more as B：視為 B 多於 A。"],["As a result, speakers…are more likely to…","be likely to V＝很可能；注意主詞為人，不可用 It is likely that 同義換位錯誤。"],["in adaptation to","為了適應…；adapt to / in response to 概念相近。"],["habitual / trivial","habitual 習慣性的；trivial 瑣碎的、微不足道的（far from a trivial habit）。"],["解題技巧","先找代名詞（This tendency / For them / These differences）指回哪句，再看轉折詞（In contrast / however）。"]],c:"主題：與機器交談（thank you）反映人類溝通模式。選項庫共用 (A)–(E)。",q:[
"<b>【31–34】</b>\nTalking to machines has become a familiar part of modern life. Many people now give voice commands to digital assistants, ask chatbots questions, or even say “thank you” after receiving help. To some, this behavior may appear unnecessary, since machines are not capable of feelings. To others, however, it reflects deeper patterns in human communication.\nThroughout history, people have adjusted their language according to their audience. When speaking to children or pets, for instance, they often simplify their speech and adopt a gentler tone. [31] As devices become more responsive and human-like, users have begun to treat them less as tools and more as social partners. This shift, in turn, raises questions about whether such interactions are merely habitual or carry broader implications.\nCultural context also plays a significant role in shaping these interactions. In societies where politeness is highly valued, individuals are taught to show respect in nearly all forms of communication. As a result, speakers from these backgrounds are more likely to use polite expressions when addressing machines. [32] These differences suggest that the way people communicate with machines is influenced not only by technological design but also by social expectations.\nAge is another factor that helps explain this phenomenon. Younger users, having grown up surrounded by digital devices, tend to interact with machines in a more natural and conversational manner. Older generations, by contrast, may see such behavior as unnecessary or even unusual. [33] This contrast highlights how experience shapes attitudes.\nWhile it may appear simple on the surface, talking to machines is far from a trivial habit. [34] As technology advances, such interactions are likely to play an even more significant role in the way people communicate.",[31,"…speak to children or pets, they simplify speech and adopt a gentler tone. ___ As devices become more human-like…",B2,0,"(A) This tendency 指前文的調整語言習慣，extended to machines 銜接後句。"],
[32,"…speakers from polite cultures are more likely to use polite expressions with machines. ___ These differences suggest…",B2,4,"後句 These differences 需前有對比；(E) In contrast 提出重視效率的文化。"],
[33,"…Older generations may see such behavior as unnecessary or even unusual. ___ This contrast highlights how experience shapes attitudes.",B2,3,"(D) For them 指年長世代，與年輕人形成對比。"],
[34,"…talking to machines is far from a trivial habit. ___ As technology advances…",B2,2,"(C) 總結全文主題：溝通方式隨新環境而演變。"]]},
{t:"五、閱讀測驗",n:[["linear model / notion","linear 線性的；notion 概念 —— 與 view、perspective 同屬「看法」類字（第 36 題）。"],["since it is already known and therefore “visible”","since 因為＋therefore 因此，連接已知→可見的因果。"],["Rather than being a universal truth, this way of thinking is simply one of many possible interpretations","Rather than + V-ing：而不是…；one of many + 複數名詞。"],["elusive","難以捉摸、難以發現的（＝hard to find）。"],["render + O + C","rendered the forts obsolete：使堡壘過時／失效；obsolete＝過時的。"],["…bastions that are arranged to create a distinctive star-shaped outline","that 關係子句；arranged to V＝被安排以便…。"],["Defenders stationed in one bastion could fire…, ensuring that every inch was covered","過去分詞 stationed 後置修飾；ensuring… 為分詞構句，表結果。"],["flanking fire / crossfire","側翼火力／交叉火力。"],["moat / blind spot","護城河；視線死角。"]],q:[
"<b>【35–38】</b>\nWhy do we imagine time as moving forward? In everyday language, people often describe the future as something “ahead” of them and the past as something “behind.” This linear model seems natural, yet it is not universal. Instead, it reflects a specific way of understanding time—a notion that is shaped by both culture and experience.\nIn many Western societies, time is commonly represented as a straight line extending from the past to the future. This view is reinforced by written language, which typically moves from left to right, and by calendars that place earlier dates before later ones. In addition, visual timelines in textbooks and media often follow this same direction. As a result, people in these cultures tend to associate progress with moving forward.\nHowever, not all cultures share this perspective. In some communities, time is understood in a very different way. For instance, the Aymara people in South America describe the past as being “in front,” since it is already known and therefore “visible,” while the future lies “behind,” as it cannot yet be seen. Similar patterns have been observed in other regions, suggesting that this understanding is not unique. These contrasts indicate that the direction of time is not fixed but rather depends on how people relate to knowledge, memory, and uncertainty.\nAnother factor that shapes this understanding is the human body itself. People naturally move forward when they walk, and this physical motion may influence how they perceive time. Gestures also play a role: when talking about the future, speakers often point ahead, while references to the past may be accompanied by a backward gesture. Because of this, the idea of “moving into the future” fits people’s natural intuition. Yet this explanation alone cannot account for all variations. These differences show that cultural patterns and bodily experience work together to shape how time is imagined.\nIn the end, the way people describe time reveals more about human perception than about time itself. What seems obvious in one culture may appear unfamiliar in another. Rather than being a universal truth, this way of thinking is simply one of many possible interpretations, and it may continue to change as societies and technologies advance.",[35,"What does placing the past “in front” suggest about that culture’s view of time?",["Future events are considered more predictable than past events.","Time is understood as something that can be directly observed in space.","The past is given greater importance because it can be clearly perceived.","Spatial direction is assigned based on whether events are known or unknown."],3,"Aymara 人以「已知／可見」決定前後；(C) 誘答，文中未說過去較重要。"],
[36,"Which set of words refers to the concept of how time is imagined?",["view, model, notion, perspective","future, past, direction, movement","culture, experience, language, body","truth, explanation, motion, perception"],0,"這些字皆為「理解事物的方式」的同義概念。"],

"<b>【39–42】</b>\nFew African animals are as mysterious as an aardvark. Although this mammal lives across much of sub-Saharan Africa, little is known about its behavior. Unlike other well-known African animals, aardvarks rarely appear in wildlife photographs. Yet, there is much more to this little-known animal than meets the eye.\nOne reason aardvarks are so memorable is their distinctive appearance, which makes them look like a mixture of swine, rabbits and kangaroos. They have long, narrow snouts that help locate food through an excellent sense of smell. Their large ears resemble those of rabbits, while their thick tails and sturdy bodies give them a unique shape. An adult aardvark may grow to nearly two meters in length and weigh as much as 80 kilograms. Its powerful claws are specially adapted for digging through hard soil and creating underground burrows. Such physical adaptations help shape both the aardvark’s appearance and its underground lifestyle.\nDespite living in many parts of Africa, aardvarks are surprisingly difficult to spot. They are active mainly at night and spend much of the day inside burrows. In addition, they usually live alone and leave few visible signs of their presence. Even experienced wildlife researchers may spend years without seeing one in their natural habitat. Because direct observations are uncommon, people still know relatively little about their daily life and social behavior. For these reasons, aardvarks are often described as <b>elusive</b> animals.\nAlthough aardvarks seldom appear in wildlife or nature documentaries, they are more important than their low profile might suggest. In some African folk tales, they are associated with determination and hard work because of their digging habits. Scientists are also interested in how aardvarks contribute to local ecosystems. Their burrows provide shelter for many animals, including reptiles, small mammals, and birds, especially during extreme weather conditions. Many questions about these animals remain unanswered, but as we learn more about aardvarks, people can gain a deeper appreciation for one of Africa’s most unusual mammals.",[39,"Which question is mainly answered in the third paragraph?",["How have aardvarks adapted to underground living?","Why have aardvarks become endangered in recent years?","Why are aardvarks viewed negatively in some folk tales?","Why is so little known about aardvarks despite their wide distribution in Africa?"],3,"夜行、白天躲洞穴、獨居，因此難觀察、所知有限。"],

"<b>【43–46】</b>\nAmong the most remarkable military structures ever built, star forts are instantly recognizable for their clever geometric design. Unlike the tall, round towers of medieval castles, they feature pointed parts called bastions that are arranged to create a distinctive star-shaped outline when viewed from above. This revolutionary design emerged in 15th-century Italy, where military engineers sought new ways to defend against an increasingly powerful threat: the cannon.\nTraditional circular fortifications had a critical weakness. They created blind spots at the base of their walls, where attackers could take shelter out of the defenders’ reach. Star forts addressed this in two key ways. First, the outward-pointing bastions eliminated blind spots entirely. Defenders stationed in one bastion could fire along the curtain wall toward the next, ensuring that every inch of the exterior was covered. This tactic was known as “crossfire” or “flanking fire.” No attacker could approach without being exposed. Second, star fort walls were built low and thick, often from packed earth rather than stone; these angled surfaces caused cannonballs to bounce off or sink harmlessly into the ground. Additional defensive features strengthened these forts further. A wide moat, or a wide channel of water, often surrounded the structure to prevent attackers from tunneling beneath the walls. Inside, an open central courtyard provided space for organizing troops and storing supplies, supporting operations during prolonged conflicts.\nDuring the 16th and 17th centuries, the star fort spread rapidly across Europe and into colonial territories. The Dutch, renowned for their engineering expertise and extensive global trade networks, constructed such forts everywhere from Taiwan to South Africa. In Tainan, the ruins of Fort Zeelandia, built in the 1620s, still attract visitors today. Similarly, European powers erected star forts along the coasts of India, Sri Lanka, and the Americas to guard their overseas trading interests. By the 19th century, however, advances in weapons had <b>rendered even the strongest star forts obsolete</b>, quietly bringing this era of geometric fortification to a close.",[43,"What question can the passage answer?",["How were star forts used in 20th-century warfare?","Where is the largest star fort in the world located?","Why was the star-shaped design of these forts created?","Who was the most famous architect to design a star fort?"],2,"首段說明因應「火炮威脅」而出現。"],
"<img src='data:image/jpeg;base64,'>",[44,"Which statement about the parts (A)–(D) of the star fort picture is correct?",["Part (A) created blind spots where attackers could hide safely.","Part (B) was the section covered by flanking fire.","Part (C) was used for storing food and military supplies.","Part (D) served as an underground escape tunnel."],1,"(B) 是稜堡間的城牆（curtain wall），受側翼火力覆蓋；(A) 稜堡消除死角；(C) 護城河；(D) 中央庭院。"],
[45,"Which can be inferred about star forts in the colonial era?",["Star forts built overseas were smaller and less effective than those in Europe.","Fort Zeelandia was abandoned shortly after it was built due to local resistance.","European nations used star forts to establish and protect their presence abroad.","The Dutch were the only European power to construct star forts outside Europe."],2,"歐洲列強在印度、斯里蘭卡、美洲建堡壘，保護海外貿易利益。"],

"<b>【47–50】</b>\nSeveral years ago, a CNN news report drew global attention to Taiwan’s pedestrian safety problems. The report harshly described Taiwan as a difficult place for pedestrians and pulled no punches in portraying the country’s traffic environment rather than softening its language. Since then, the government has taken measures to improve road safety. However, many people continue to debate both the causes of the problem and whether the current reforms are addressing the right issues, as shown in the following forum discussion.\n<b>A. Alan</b>　Many drivers don’t yield even when pedestrians clearly have the right of way. Drivers need to be better educated about pedestrian safety. Laws alone have limited effects.\n<b>B. Bella</b>　Road design is the main problem. Dangerous intersections often place pedestrians and vehicles in conflict with one another.\n<b>C. Chris</b>　I support the government’s recent reforms. Higher penalties send a clear message that unsafe driving will not be tolerated.\n<b>D. Diana</b>　The reforms are a good start, but poorly designed traffic signals continue to create dangerous situations for pedestrians.\n<b>E. Ethan</b>　The real problem is weak enforcement. Rules mean little if violators are rarely punished.\n<b>F. Fiona</b>　Many pedestrians have no safe roads to use. The government should build safer sidewalks and improve crossings for pedestrians.\n<b>G. George</b>　I am not convinced that heavier penalties are the answer. In the long run, it may be more effective to teach road users than simply punish them.\n<b>H. Hannah</b>　Pedestrians also share responsibility. Some people cross roads while distracted by their phones or ignore traffic signals, so they should also learn how to protect themselves.\n<b>I. Irene</b>　The design of roads and transportation system deserves more attention in this discussion. Better design can help prevent accidents before they happen.\n<b>J. Jack</b>　There is no single cause. Driver/pedestrian behavior, infrastructure, enforcement, and urban planning all play important roles.",[47,"Despite recent legal reforms aimed at improving road safety, participants on the forum still hold different perspectives: Some call for better <u>(47)</u> to help road users become more aware of safety issues, others believe that poor road design should be to blame, and still others argue that existing traffic rules must be strictly <u>(48)</u>.","education",0,"Alan、George 皆強調教育；better 後接名詞 education。","t"],
[48,"…existing traffic rules must be strictly ___.","enforced",0,"Ethan 提到 enforcement；rules 被執行 → 過去分詞 enforced。","t"],

George","H. Hannah","I. Irene","J. Jack"],[1,3,5,8],"B 道路設計、D 交通號誌、F 人行道與穿越設施、I 道路與交通系統設計。A、G 教育；C、E 執法；H 責任；J 多重因素。","m"],
